newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - following Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - following Singapore.

text.p: Gulf oil product prices have risen in line with the Singapore market and it will be Asia demand again that sways short-term price direction in the Gulf, traders in the region said on Thursday.

Gulf middle distillate prices have moved up on tighter Asian availability, helped by Indonesian and Chinese buying, with gas oil gaining 85 cents in the week to stand at $24.35 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday.
Premiums to independent price quotes remain unchanged with kerosene holding up at 30-40 cents and gas oil at 50-55 cents but still below the year-on-year $1.00-$1.20 comparison.
Naphtha is also resilient at a $12-15 premium to quotes.
"Indonesia is back in the market and India has come for its terms supplies (of superior kerosene and diesel)...It's delaying the downturn at least," said one trader.
Heavy gas oil buying by a Singapore trader had also buoyed markets for March and April delivery.
India's IOC has issed a one year-term tender to buy superior kerosene for delivery from May to April 1998 and also for 0.25-0.50-and-1.0 percent sulphur gas oil. These close March 13.
Pakistan is also looking to take up 420,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent gas oil between April and June.
"We're seeing very good demand from the region (Indian sub-continent) but I question how may of these cargoes will be directly sourced from the Middle East," said one trader.
Other tenders in the market included a buying tender from state-owned Saudi Aramco for up to 1.5 million barrels of 95-octane gasoline for April delivery, traders said.
"It's more signs that the product balances (in Saudi Arabia) can get off line and demand is running at good steam," one trader in the region said.
Qatar is also expected to tender for the sale of products for second quarter delivery.
Supplies from Oman will be disrupted by maintenance work at its single refinery.
Gulf bunker fuel markets are also expected to stay in current ranges at $98-100 a tonne for 380-cst Fujairah bunkers because of upbeat shipping demand in the region, traders said.
